rationale: Objective is ttft_ms for the interactive workload: the t0->t1 interval is prefill forward + first-token argmax + explicit 'first-token-ready' synchronize on a single leased RTX 4090. The torch collector already ran and resolved attribution completely (66441/66441 kernels associated, 0 unassociated, 0 ambiguous forward sequences), so nsys adds nothing: no overlap, graph-tracing, or attribution question remains open. The single remaining diagnostic question for TTFT is how the t0->t1 interval decomposes into GPU compute, host dispatch/launch gaps, and synchronization wait for an eager batch=1 BF16 SDPA Qwen3-4B forward over 36 layers. execution_timeline supplies exactly the missing dimensions: a separate plain Torch trace with CPU-to-CUDA submit associations, per-device intervals, and synchronization boundaries, which reveals whether the GPU idles between layer submissions and how long the explicit first-token-ready sync actually waits (acknowledging that GPU readiness/consumer completion may remain unknown and clock alignment bounds apply only to matched CPU submissions). python_runtime adds a warmed cProfile view of host dispatch and binding costs to attribute Python-side overhead in the eager forward loop, accepted as perturbing and not a clean performance score or GPU duration. nccl_tuning, collective_calibration, and device_telemetry are excluded: no communication exists (single device), the workload is GPU-resident so device-wide NVML rate samples cannot attribute TTFT, and collective_calibration is only a reference experiment for comms. candidate_diagnostics and binding_cost are excluded because no candidate exists yet; binding_cost also reports only whole-invocation parent-vs-passthrough cost and belongs in later candidate resource feedback. All GPU measurements remain in the framework's leased workers; any CPU-side inspection uses /root/autodl-tmp/dev-venv/bin/python per worker-environment.json.
